subject: geography
source_note: Topic structure follows the IB Diploma Geography guide. HL students study three optional themes, the three-unit core 'global change', and the HL extension 'global interactions' (Units 4-6). Topic names are guide-accurate; connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (the IB does not publish these).

connections.why: The key concepts (place, scale, power) frame every core unit
Fieldwork applies the cartographic and data skills directly
Climate data interpretation depends on graphical and statistical skills
A growing, urbanising population drives resource demand
Fossil-fuel resource consumption is the main driver of climate change
Climate change reshapes the world's extreme environments
Warming and sea-level rise transform coastal and ocean systems
Population growth and migration drive urbanisation
Population pressure shapes food demand and health outcomes
Water is a key resource whose security the core examines
Freshwater availability underpins agriculture and food security
Hazard risk depends on where and how densely people live
Cities concentrate vulnerability to geophysical hazards
Extreme environments are increasingly tourism destinations
Tourism and sport reshape urban places and economies
Ocean fisheries are a major global food source
Cities are centres of intense resource consumption and waste
Control of resources is a foundation of global power
Population patterns underpin uneven human development
Power asymmetries shape who benefits from global development
Global networks of power generate geopolitical and economic risk
Local responses to globalisation build (or undermine) resilience
Climate change is a central environmental risk in the HL extension
Global cities are nodes in networks of power and flows
Urban environments are a common context for fieldwork investigations
